name: POST /mcp answers its newest version to one it does not speak

serverInfo.name: optionality
serverInfo.title: optionality — an SPX options book, read-only

result.instructions: Read-only access to one trader's SPX options book: what is held, the rules (Monitors) that watch it, their histories, the Reference securities on the page and the service's own health. Nothing here adds, edits, mutes, deletes, records or closes anything. Every successful tool answers one JSON object: `source`, the API's own GET it served; `read_at`, when the service read it, in the service's display zone; and `data`, that GET's body exactly as the HTTP API serves it (keys sorted). The LIVE tools ask the market-data Provider, which allows 60 calls per 30 seconds shared with the alarm sweep and the dashboard. Three (holdings, watchlist, references) read only what the service already watches: their answers are shared by every caller for 5 seconds, so asking again sooner returns the same answer with the same `read_at` — there is no point polling faster. The fourth, price_spreads, prices ANY SPX structure you name, in one bounded call: the same structures asked again within 5 seconds are answered from the same call, and the service makes at most a capped number of such calls in any 30 seconds whoever asks (12 unless the owner set otherwise) — past it the tool error says how many seconds to wait, so price several structures in ONE call rather than one per call. Prices are in index points per contract unless a field says money; P&L is money. A failed read is a tool error carrying the service's own words.
